actions.action: Check soil moisture 2-3 inches deep with a finger before watering
Unpot the plant, shake off wet soil and inspect roots and rhizome
Cut away black, mushy or smelly roots/rhizome with alcohol-wiped scissors if present
Repot in a pot with drainage holes using chunky aroid mix (or potting soil with perlite and orchid bark), rhizome at soil level
Set the draining pot inside the decorative metal pot
Place the plant in bright indirect light near the window
Remove dead leaves at the base as they die

reason: The answer correctly flags poor drainage and recommends repotting with drainage and light near the window, but its main diagnosis is overwatering/root rot when the plant actually needed more water and was root-bound; the soil check keeps the watering advice from being harmful.
